hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A range is good if at least k pairs of identical elements occur inside it.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Track identical value occurrences using frequency maps while moving a dynamic boundary.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: For each right index, advance the left boundary while pair count remains at least k.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

def countGood(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    count = Counter()
    ans = 0
    left = 0
    cur_pairs = 0
    for right, x in enumerate(nums):
        cur_pairs += count[x]
        count[x] += 1
        while cur_pairs >= k:
            ans += len(nums) - right
            count[nums[left]] -= 1
            cur_pairs -= count[nums[left]]
            left += 1
    return ans
```

complexity.notes: Both pointers traverse the array at most once, maintaining current pair count in O(1).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(n^2) pairs directly takes quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores frequency table in O(n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Maintains running combinations count C(freq, 2) dynamically.

from collections import Counter

def countGood(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    count = Counter()
    ans = 0
    left = 0
    cur_pairs = 0
    for right, x in enumerate(nums):
        cur_pairs += count[x]
        count[x] += 1
        while cur_pairs >= k:
            ans += len(nums) - right
            count[nums[left]] -= 1
            cur_pairs -= count[nums[left]]
            left += 1
    return ans
